paragraphs: Friend, this passage is about what people do when they get back what they wanted. David is home safe, and look at the three groups in front of him. Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, shows up with his feet uncared for and his mustache untrimmed, and when David offers him land, he says, "let Ziba take it all!" Why? "Since my lord the king has safely come to his own house." (2 Samuel 19:30) The king coming home was the prize. The land was just land.

Then Barzillai, eighty years old, turns down a spot at the king's side. He gave to David while David was staying at Mahanaim, and he wants nothing for it. He says, "why should the king repay me with such a reward?" (2 Samuel 19:36) I think that's a man who knows what he can still carry, and he sends Chimham in his place. Giving without keeping score is a skill, baker, and I'm still working on it. Put a cookie box on the counter and watch me count who took what.

Meanwhile, Judah and Israel are arguing over who gets more of the king, and the text says Judah "spoke more fiercely" (2 Samuel 19:43). Two groups, one king, and everybody is counting shares. Put it side by side and the lesson gets loud: some people hold on tight to what they get from the king, and some are glad just to have him home. Ask yourself, friend, which of those you are on a normal Tuesday. And this story isn't finished yet.
